title: Find the Most Competitive Subsequence
summary: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, return a subsequence of size k that is the most competitive.
statement: Given an integer array and a positive integer k, return a subsequence of size k that is the most competitive. A subsequence is more competitive if, at the first differing position, its number is less than the corresponding number in another subsequence of the same length.
constraints: Return the lexicographically smallest length-k subsequence while preserving original order.
hints: Remove a larger suffix value when the remaining input can still fill k positions.
Maintain the lexicographically smallest feasible monotonic stack prefix.
While top>current and popped length plus remaining count can reach k, pop; append while size<k.
The first differing position improves whenever a larger top is safely replaced, and the feasibility test prevents undersizing.
editorial: The first differing position improves whenever a larger top is safely replaced, and the feasibility test prevents undersizing.

tests.explanation: Discarding three and five when two arrives leaves the smallest possible prefix 2,6.
The monotonic stack produces 2,3,3,4 as the smallest feasible sequence.
